title: Next-Gen Xbox Could Be $1,800 And Launch In 2028 – Report
description: A new report sheds more details on Microsoft's plans for new Xbox hardware, including a new handheld device and console, and one of the biggest takeaways is the alleged price. According to Fortune, the Project Helix console could cost between $1,200 and $1,800, unless Microsoft opts to subsidize the cost. The system could launch in 2028, the report said. It's not uncommon for platform-holders to eat some of the cost of a new console and make up the difference with software and services. When the Xbox Series X and S platforms launched in 2020, then-Xbox CEO Phil Spencer said Microsoft was losing as much as $200 on every console it sold. Project Helix might be very expensive. Part of what might be driving up the price for new consoles is the ongoing AI-fueled memory and component shortages. Microsoft itself is one of the biggest proponents of the build-out of all things AI, so its own efforts are contributing to an environment where the next Xbox could be incredibly expensive. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma reacted to this irony, saying it's "wonderful" that GPUs have use beyong gaming. Richer households already made up the majority of console-buyers today, and that trend is expected to continue Additionally, the report said Microsoft might release a "next-generation handheld device" for Xbox by the end of 2027, though there were no details on pricing or anything else. Project Helix is the name for Microsoft's efforts for a "family of devices," so that would seemingly span both console and handheld. The report added that Microsoft's Xbox and Windows teams reportedly battled over what software should run Project Helix, with the Windows team wanting the handheld to use a "trimmed-down" version of Windows Home. The Xbox team, meanwhile, reportedly pushed to build its own dedicated software. An unnamed "senior Xbox executive" was said to have threatened to pull the plug on the entire handheld device rather than use Windows. Going forward, Xbox is "largely controlling the…

title: Here Are The Mechanics and Dozens Of New Cards From Magic: The Gathering’s Star Trek Set
description: After a year that featured alternate realities, ninja turtles, superheroes, and hobbits, the final Magic: The Gathering expansion of 2026 is going where no Universes Beyond set has gone before, as Star Trek is scheduled to launch in November. Today, Wizards of the Coast revealed the mechanics players can expect in the set, along with dozens of new cards from both the main set and the preconstructed Commander decks. We also got a glimpse at some of the set's special treatments, including the seven cards that will come signed by the people depicted on the artwork. Here's everything revealed during today's Magic: The Gathering Star Trek debut. The mechanics of MTG Star Trek Seven new mechanics--two of them found only in the Commander cards--highlight the set, along with a eighth mechanic returning from 2024's Edge of Eternities. OPen Communications First is Beam Me Up, which allows you to cast certain spells from your graveyard by returning a creature you control to its owner's hand and paying a separate cost. The example card provided is Open Communications, which normally costs a single blue mana, but you can cast it again from your graveyard by returning a creature to its owner's hand and paying two generic and one blue mana. Next is Face A Dilemma, which adds an additional wrinkle to a mechanic Magic fans are very familiar with. Basically, any time you have to choose a mode in a spell, you are "facing a dilemma," and there are cards in Star Trek that will give extra benefits simply because you made a choice. Seven of Nine, for example, lets you draw a card any time you have to make a choice on a modal spell. Star Trek also introduces new modal spells, like the enchantment Kobayashi Maru Scenario. Every turn after casting this card, you must choose one of the four effects listed on the card, and you can't choose the same one twice--which means if you can't remove the enchantment after four turns, it's game over. The next mechanic is Federation, which cares about…

title: Xbox Series X|S Is Getting A Surprise Graphics Boost From AMD
description: Sony isn't the only company introducing new upscaling technology to its flagship PlayStation 5, as Microsoft and AMD have announced that FSR 4.1 is coming to more devices--including Xbox Series X|S consoles--in the future. Similar to Sony's hardware-accelerated upscaling solutions for PS5 and PS5 Pro, AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution (FSR) 4.1 is an advanced, machine-learning-based temporal image upscaling and reconstruction technology that can render a game at a lower resolution and then upscale it to a higher resolution. While it's highly doubtful that Xbox Series X|S consoles will start offering PS5 Pro-like graphics (both consoles lack dedicated hardware for machine-learning algorithms), this should still give owners a noticeable bump in graphical quality and performance if implemented properly. "At Xbox, we're building a gaming platform designed to meet players where they are and make it easier for creators to reach them," Xbox chief technology officer Scott Van Vliet said in the announcement video. "AMD has been an important partner in that journey for more than two decades. Together, our teams have been pushing gaming forward, across Xbox and Windows, from the silicon at the heart of our consoles and handhelds to technologies like DirectX, Advanced Shader Delivery, and Auto SR that help developers get more from the hardware and deliver better experiences for our players. Today, we're excited to take another step forward together, with FSR 4.1 coming to Xbox." Van Vliet added that FSR 4.1 will come to Xbox Series X|S "soon," and that Microsoft and AMD are working to bring the tech to the next-gen Xbox console, Project Helix. Beyond that, AMD didn't share any more details on FSR 4.1 for Xbox Series X|S. FSR 1 and FSR 2 relied primarily on spatial algorithms or basic temporal accumulation to upscale games, and questions remain about who will adopt the technology and add support. Just because the latest version of FSR is out doesn't mean a game will automatically…

title: This Character-Action Zombie Game Stumbles Into Its Own Way
description: Stupid Never Dies makes a strong, if extremely weird, first impression. Wrapping roguelite progression around the system of an action-RPG and setting that story in an inventive punk-inspired world of monsters is an inviting hook. Plus, it's hard not to feel some affection for the dimwitted hero and his undoubtedly creepy quest to revive the supposed love of his afterlife. But the inventive world and a few neat ideas can only carry this game so far, and I ultimately struggled to look past the repetitive and often imprecise combat. The world of Stupid Never Dies has been completely taken over by monsters who emerged from inside the Earth's crust. These monsters are very conspicuously inspired by classic silver screen incarnations and popular B-movies, all filtered through a '90s or '00s pop-punk aesthetic. It's a stylish blend of influences that immediately identifies this game's goofball, self-effacing tone. Stupid Never Dies When these monsters took over the world, they all but wiped out humanity. In the aftermath, a new caste system emerged, with zombies considered to be little more than cannon fodder in the fight for monster supremacy. Zombies who refused to fight in the war are seen as even lower than that--protagonist Davy is one of those, a teenage-looking undead who's more of a lover than a fighter. In fact, Davy shambles his way into the adventure accidentally. He's just hungry, and happens to eat a weird glowing egg he finds laying around. This turns out to be a Phoenix Egg, giving him the ability to absorb power from other monsters. He doesn't really care to use this newfound power until an associate, Dr. Frank, tells him he may be able to use it to revive a dead girl named Julia who he's been infatuated with. Julia is a random human that Davy found in a freezer, and Davy sets his sights on reviving her solely because he imagines they would be a happy couple. This motivation doesn't give Julia any agency--we don't know whether she would even want to date a…

title: Call Of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 DMZ Tips
description: Modern Warfare 4's DMZ is now available in early access, bringing major upgrades to Call of Duty's PvPvE extraction mode. In this guide, we'll provide some tips for leveling up, surviving the harsh map environments, and making the most of your DMZ storage space. Matches of DMZ allow for up to 60 players in trios, and you're tasked with surviving and extracting in a PvPvE environment. You have 30 minutes of match time before a deadly circle of irradiated gas floods the map, and then you'll have a final 10-minute timer to escape via one of the map's exfil locations. As with most extraction shooters, dying in DMZ means losing everything, making it a high-risk for high-reward game mode. The choice is yours for how you want to approach a match of DMZ, but there are several things you'll want to know before loading into the dangerous world of Hajin. Do your DMZ orders DMZ Orders shown on Tac Map DMZ orders are the first mission types you are introduced to in DMZ. There are several pages of these tutorial-style objectives, but don't disregard these for their simplicity, as they are still worth completing for the XP needed to rank up and unlock better gear and equipment. Don't forget FOB upgrades 3D printer FOB upgrades Your FOB is your home base, and this is where you go between DMZ matches. The DMZ Orders mentioned above will guide you through scavenging your equipment and unlocking new FOB stations. Once you've unlocked the 3D Printer station at level 2, you'll also be able to pay cash to upgrade your FOB over time, including bigger stash upgrades and larger bank storage. Make sure to make these important upgrades as soon as you can, as you're just losing money if you don't have enough bank storage to hold it all. description: Modern Warfare 4's DMZ is now available in early access, bringing major upgrades to Call of Duty's extraction mode. This iteration of DMZ has in-depth story missions, side objectives, and plenty of opportunities for exploration. The mission types and match selections can be a bit confusing, so this guide will explain each mission type and what you should choose before loading into a match of DMZ. MW4 DMZ mission types explained Matches of DMZ allow for up to 60 players in trios, and you're tasked with surviving and extracting. You have 30 minutes of matchtime before a deadly circle of irradiated gas floods the map, and then you'll have a final 10-minute timer to escape via one of the map's exfil locations. As a beginner, DMZ throws out the names of several different mission types, and each one is drastically different in how they affect your match of DMZ. DMZ Orders DMZ Orders objective examples At first, DMZ sounds like your story missions, but these are actually a larger continuation of the tutorial mission, and they are designed to teach you how to scavenge, craft items, and upgrade your FOB. These are the first missions you'll have access to when loading into DMZ, and they can be completed at any time for XP. These missions are tailored story objectives located at specific POIs across Hajin, but there is enough freedom to allow for various strategies and replayability when tackling these missions. Completing these missions earns you DMZ XP and rewards. There are currently six story missions at launch, and you must choose a specific story mission during the infil selection of the FOB. title: Sony Boss: “Creativity Is For Humans, Not AI”
description: Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick and Sony Group President and CEO, Hiroki Totoki, commented on the future of gaming today at the Paley International Summit. Naturally, the topic of AI came up, and Totoki believes AI technologies will not replace humans in game development, in part because of the creativity required. "Creativity is for humans, not AI,” Totoki said, as reported by IGN. “How to use the technology profile is important. Of course, I encourage my people to use AI in a certain manner, but at [the] same time we try to keep the rights and rights holders and creators and artists.” For his part, Zelnick said it's his belief that AI itself will not replace a developer, but instead, people who don't embrace AI might be replaced by people who do. "I’m fond of saying AI is a collection of datasets, compute, and large language models. That’s what it is. And datasets, by definition, are backward-looking. That’s all they are. And creativity, at its best, is forward-looking," he said. Zelnick said ideas that are "completely unexpected" don't come from algorithms--they come from creative people making surprising, original choices. To make his point, Zelnick said when he was an executive at Fox, he oversaw the release of Home Alone, a movie that no one expected to be a success. "It turned out to be the highest-grossing comedy of all time. So if hits are unexpected, data sets aren’t gonna get you there, no matter how fluent they are," he said. Both PlayStation and Take-Two have embraced AI, with PlayStation heavily leveraging the technology in its game-development processes. As for Take-Two, the publisher is utilizing the technology for its workflows, but there is no AI in GTA 6. There has been significant pushback for AI in game development from developers and players alike, with many expressing concerns about job security, legal issues, and simply the further "enshi**ification" of everything they love.

title: 10 Years After The Switch 1 Reveal, I Still Haven’t Played A Game At A Rooftop Party
description: It's now been a full decade since Nintendo announced the first Switch, which is almost hard to believe, given how fresh that reveal trailer still feels in our heads. Heaps of hype and a lack of information from Nintendo about its Wii U successor, codenamed "NX," led to the company's fanbase becoming increasingly restless. Reports and rumors pointed to the NX as a console-handheld hybrid, but Nintendo didn't fully unveil the Switch until October 20, 2016 (an announcement preluded by a photo of Mario being a creep ). The three-and-a-half-minute video made it clear how Nintendo wanted players to interact with the Switch, showing several scenarios where people take their games on the go. Rewatching that trailer today, it's amusing to look back at how Nintendo foresaw the social impact of the Switch. Some moments from the trailer manifested in reality, while others were hilariously exaggerated. You have a guy taking his dog (and his copy of The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild) out on a walk, a traveler playing Skyrim on a plane and putting the game on his television upon his arrival home, and professional Splatoon players practicing before their big moment on stage. And then, there's "Nintendo Karen." The most-talked-about moment in the trailer centered on a woman playing Super Mario Odyssey before being prompted to join friends for a rooftop party (a typical gathering of millennials, as people would joke back then), during which she breaks out the Switch, pulls out that dinky little kickstand, and plays a game with a friend as onlookers holding red Solo cups watch with indifference. Fans branded this commercial character as "Karen" and debated the social implications of bringing a Switch to such a function. The Nintendo Switch reveal trailer remains a striking piece of marketing, with its upbeat vibe and extra emphasis on the Switch's branding (much needed, after the Wii U's marketing failures). In the years since the Switch's release, I’ve seen Switches out in the…

title: Xbox Game Pass’s Newest Wave Is Headlined By A Huge Final Fantasy Adventure
description: Right on schedule, the second wave of games coming to Xbox Game Pass has been revealed. After the first batch, which included Gears of War: E-Day, Battlefield 6, and more, the rest of the month will add games like Final Fantasy 7 Remake and The Seance of Blake Manor to the subscription service. We've also gotten a sneak peek at what's coming in November, so there's plenty to play over the next couple of weeks. As a reminder, several games are also leaving Xbox Game Pass this month, including a pair of Double Fine classics and one massive Star Wars Lego game. Final Fantasy 7 Remake Intergrade is the headline act in this new wave of arrivals, right on time for anyone looking to experience the saga from its first chapter. The Intergrade version includes the original game and its Yuffie-centric expansion, but you'll have to wait until October 29 to embark on the Unknown Journey. Before then, you can grab the Game Preview edition of Sandustry on PC starting October 21. A game about exploration and automation, it's a tempting download for anyone who enjoys assembly-line video games. You can also get Dodo Duckie on October 22, a reality-bending odyssey where you'll get to outsmart aliens and solve puzzles while wielding duck powers, and October 26 will see the MMO-lite action RPG Scramble Knights Online make its day-one debut on Game Pass. The Séance of Blake Manor was one of GameSpot's favorite games of 2025, and you can check out this supernatural detective mystery for yourself when it's added to the Game Pass library on October 27. Starting October 29, you can explore Midgar in the aforementioned Final Fantasy 7 Remake Intergrade, play classic Plants vs. Zombies in HD, and the horror-parkour game Terrible Lizards is another day-one release to round out the month. Looking ahead, November will kick off with Pit of Goblin, an online horror co-op adventure in which you play as a scrappy goblin. title: Netflix’s Push Into Gaming Continues To Fall Short
description: Netflix has undertaken efforts over the years to increase its footprint in the world of video games, but it's been a bumpy road, and new data suggests that the company is falling short of its targets. According to a Netflix memo seen by The Wall Street Journal, only 3.5% of Netflix's subscribers play games monthly. That's 10% behind Netflix's 2026 target for "reach and engagement" for games, the memo said. In 2022, it was reported that fewer than 1% of Netflix subscribers played games on Netflix. Getting deeper into games is part of Netflix's effort to increase engagement, and it's not the only measure that Netflix has undertaken. The company has also expanded to live sports and podcasts. Netflix's priorities for gaming have bounced around over the years. At one point in time, Netflix was planning to create AAA games and hired big-name talent. However, Netflix later backtracked, and today the company focuses more on mobile and social games. Recently, co-CEO Ted Sarandos was asked if Netflix will abandon gaming entirely in the future, and he doesn't think the company will, at least not soon. Sarandos said gaming is appealing to Netflix because, for example, someone who just finished a Netflix show can stay engaged with the brand through Netflix's tie-in games connected to those franchises. Beyond tie-in games for Netflix properties like Stranger Things and Love is Blind, Netflix commissions new games like Unhinged and The Conjuring: Unspoken. The streaming giant also made a big play in gaming this year by hosting the GTA 6 Extended Look trailer, and it worked to get people to sign up for Netflix and watch on the platform. Netflix previously worked with Take-Two to bring GTA games to the platform. Red Dead Redemption from Take-Two's Rockstar division remains available to play on Netflix. These new details about Netflix's efforts in gaming come amidst a big shakeup at the company--a number of top executives were let go, or left, earlier this week ahead of Netflix's…
